paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: prayer is for the person who knows God is listening. David doesn't mumble. He lays his plea before the LORD at daybreak and waits "in expectation" (Psalm 5:3). He isn't hoping somebody might pick up. He's talking to "my King and my God" (Psalm 5:2).

Now watch what gets David through the door. He says he will enter God's house "by the abundance of Your loving devotion" (Psalm 5:7). Not by his résumé, and not by his best day. That's GOOD news for a stamper who was once a quarter in a bin, because the welcome never depended on how sharp my edges were.

So David asks to be led, and he says the LORD's way is what he wants made straight before him (Psalm 5:8). Then he lands on the promise: "For surely You, O LORD, bless the righteous; You surround them with the shield of Your favor" (Psalm 5:12). Baker, take your worries to Him early, take your refuge in Him, and let Him do the leading. Nobody has ever been safer than somebody standing behind THAT shield.
